inputKind: Public researcher-authored source summaries and limitations; not full documents

documents.title: AISHE Report 2023-24
documents.text: 48,246 colleges were registered and 46,468 responded. Of responding colleges, 17.1% were government, 12.9% private aided and 70.0% private unaided. Contains state tables for private/government colleges and district distribution. Responding-college percentages must not be applied as exact counts to all registered colleges. Institution prevalence is not a funding share.

documents.title: Union Ministry releases AISHE 2022-23 and 2023-24 reports
documents.text: For 2023-24, 59,533 of 64,756 registered HEIs participated. Higher education enrolment is reported as 4.50 crore in 2023-24. GER is 30 in 2023-24 and uses ages 18-23 population projections based on Census 2011. Participation is voluntary and data is self-reported by institutions. Registration, survey response and estimated enrolment have different denominators. Report reference period differs from publication date.

documents.title: AISHE Final Reports
documents.text: Lists 2023-24 and 2022-23 final reports and Excel files. Index page is a discovery source, not a transaction or district funding ledger.

documents.title: Akshaya Patra Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Foundation describes PM POSHAN implementation for government/government-aided schools. Report says FY 2024–25 operations cover 16 states and 3 UTs. Government contributions are reported as ₹42,093.64 lakh and total income ₹85,746.61 lakh. New kitchens include Bengaluru locations, Pilerne in Goa and Kanpur. Government contributions include Anganwadi nutrition; not all school funding. Government contribution is within total income; avoid double counting. Kitchen city coverage is not equivalent to school-recipient district or a grant amount. States/cities arrays are documented examples, not full footprint.

documents.title: Azim Premji University Bengaluru Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Report identifies the university as not-for-profit, private and established under a Karnataka Act. Azim Premji Foundation is named sponsoring body. Report provides institutional teaching and research context. No university donation or scholarship amount validated in this extraction. Private university status does not imply eligibility for private equity distribution. Do not generalize one institution's funding arrangements to all private colleges.

documents.title: Five years, 10 states: Where India's government school count fell the most
documents.text: Reports uneven state-level net school-count reductions and warns against reading stock differences as a simple linear demographic story. Secondary lead, not proof of individual closures or wrongdoing. Do not import the headline as a closure-event count.

documents.title: Educate Girls FCRA financial statements for year ended 31 March 2024
documents.text: Document is financial statements prepared under FCRA for foreign contribution received and utilised. Income statement reports ₹1,08,44,95,261 donations for year ended 31 March 2024, separately from other income. Statements are signed 16 December 2024. PDF table extraction is fragmented; manually verify layout before treating each expense line as structured. Organisation-wide foreign donations do not establish donor-by-city or school-level funding. Upload path 2026 is not the fiscal year or signature date.

documents.title: Educate Girls Annual Progress Report FY 2024–25
documents.text: Audacious Project narrative identifies Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar expansion geography. FY 2024–25 report self-reports 285,237 girls enrolled through Vidya. Report describes two temporary learning centres in Prayagraj during Maha Kumbh for migrant workers' children. Programme outcomes are organisation-reported. No city-level monetary allocation established. The four named states describe a particular initiative, not necessarily the full NGO footprint. Annual programme reach cannot be summed with individual-school enrolment without deduplication.

documents.title: FCRA Online Services dashboard
documents.text: Dashboard distinguishes active/alive association count from annual returns filed across active, expired, cancelled and deemed ceased associations. State breakdown is explicitly for all association types. Registry counts are not education NGO counts or funding amounts. Snapshot may lag and uses legacy place names. Association address is not beneficiary location; do not map receipts to headquarters as local school funding.

documents.title: FCRA Online Services: Annual Returns (FC-4)
documents.text: Official portal provides FC-4 annual return filing guidance, sample form and document requirements. Portal landing page proves reporting route, not receipt by a particular school. FCRA registration or prior permission is not evidence of donation receipt or programme deployment. Sample-form fetch returned no extracted page content.

documents.title: HDFC Bank Parivartan CSR Report FY 2024–25
documents.text: CSR education work includes remedial learning, teacher training, scholarships and safe school infrastructure. ECSS supports continuation of education for economically vulnerable students. Projects implemented directly or through empanelled partners; disclosures also appear in directors' report and MCA filings. ₹1,068.03 crore report total covers all CSR sectors, not education alone; exclude from education totals. Report reach across 28 states/8 UTs refers to overall CSR, not proof of education spend in every jurisdiction. Current open scholarship applications or eligibility deadlines not verified here.

documents.title: 100 schools with zero enrolment denotified, 120 merged
documents.text: Reports 100 zero-enrolment primary/middle schools denotified and 120 primary schools with five or fewer students merged. Reports difficult-terrain and tribal-area schools were exempted from merger. Original school-wise notifications not obtained. Counts refer to different administrative actions and should remain separate. Zero enrolment and low enrolment are the official rationale reported; no matched catchment population evidence establishes a contradiction.

documents.title: Government urged to withdraw order allowing merger of low-enrolment schools
documents.text: Reports minister's statement that government has no plans to shut any government school. Reports AIDSO seeking withdrawal of a merger clause and a written assurance. Capture minister's denial alongside access concerns. School closure, transfer of classes and administrative merger may refer to different units. No inference of dishonesty or wrongdoing.

documents.title: Karnataka rolls out project to merge government schools with KPS magnet schools
documents.text: Reports a seven-school pilot linked to Honganuru KPS. Quotes circular instructions on student transfers and transport arrangements. Reports concern from educationists/student organisations about rural access. Underlying circular not retrieved in this pass. Announced/proposed state scale is not completed implementation. Allegation that a much larger number of schools would close is not adopted as a fact.

documents.title: KKR and PSP invest in Lighthouse Learning
documents.text: KKR funds invest alongside new investor PSP; KKR continues to hold a majority stake. Recipient described as an education services provider/platform. Release names presence in Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad and Delhi-NCR. No transaction amount disclosed in the primary announcement. Do not substitute media transaction estimates as primary-verified values. Equity in services platform is distinct from donations to schools, ownership of regulated educational trusts, or FCRA contributions. Presence is not proof investment proceeds were spent in every named city; Delhi NCR crosses administrative borders. Delhi-NCR presence is a regional label; it does not establish a school or spending location within Delhi's administrative boundary.

documents.title: Closure of Government Schools — Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 1374
documents.text: Annexure I reports government-school stock counts for five academic years by state/UT. Annexure II reports government-school stock counts for all Uttar Pradesh districts. India government schools: 1,022,386 in 2021-22 and 1,005,245 in 2025-26. NEP paragraph 7.4 says consolidation should only proceed when access is unaffected. The answer provides stock counts, not a school-by-school closure or merger register. Districts are not cities or school catchments. No matched population series or causal impact evaluation is provided. Reported by states/UTs through UDISE+.

documents.title: Declining Enrolment of Students in Government Schools in Uttar Pradesh — Lok Sabha Question 2445
documents.text: Provides approved central and actual released central shares for Uttar Pradesh Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI for three financial years. Shamli district government-school counts rise from 621 in 2021-22 to 623 in 2025-26. The requested district spending is answered with state-level approved/released figures; do not label these district spending. Releases are not expenditure, audited utilisation, or money received by an individual school. Annexures contain government-school counts, not verified closure events.

documents.title: National CSR Portal: company-wise project disclosures
documents.text: Schema includes project, sector, state, district, amount outlay in INR crore, amount spent in INR crore and implementation mode. Portal says company board/director reports take precedence if inconsistent. PAN India includes multiple-state projects and centralized funds. Captcha and dynamic selection prevent treating landing page as a project extract. Company registered office must not be substituted for project location. Preserve PAN India and NEC/Not Mentioned instead of distributing across states. No recipient-level totals verified.

documents.title: MCA Corporate Data Management: CSR Data
documents.text: Portal provides year, state, PSU/non-PSU and development sector filters and an implementing agency master. Displayed education sector is combined with differently abled and livelihood categories. Dynamic data values were not extracted. Do not label grouped-sector expenditure as education-only spending. Heading and filter years differ; verify downloaded report timestamp before publishing totals.

documents.title: Cabinet approves MERITE with ₹4,200 crore outlay
documents.text: Scheme targets 175 engineering institutions and 100 polytechnics. Total financial implication is ₹4,200 crore, including ₹2,100 crore World Bank loan assistance. Government/government-aided technical institutions are expected to be selected. National eligibility is not proof every city or state has an awarded institution. Targets are planned benefits, not realized outcomes. World Bank share is part of total and must not be added again.

documents.title: Cabinet approves PM SHRI Schools
documents.text: Total project cost ₹27,360 crore, including central share ₹18,128 crore, over five years. Targets more than 14,500 existing schools managed by central/state/UT/local government. Selection uses eligibility checks and challenge mode. Multi-year programme outlay is not current-year expenditure or total India education funding. Not a grant programme for all private unaided schools. National targets do not verify city-level awards.

documents.title: PM Schools for Rising India — scheme information
documents.text: At the page's update, 12,079 schools had been selected through four phases. Confirms ₹27,360 crore total and ₹18,128 crore central project cost. Selection snapshot is dated November 2024 and must not be labelled current in October 2026.

documents.title: PM-USHA: Building Stronger Institutions for a Knowledge-Driven Future
documents.text: Scheme outlay ₹12,926.10 crore for 2023-24 to 2025-26. First two PAB meetings approved 440 units worth ₹5,613.12 crore. FY 2025-26 budget stated as ₹1,815 crore. Eight new model degree college units approved across Nagaland (4), Manipur (2), Meghalaya (2), totaling ₹119.98 crore. Outlay, PAB approvals and annual budget are distinct stages and cannot be added together. A unit is not necessarily a unique institution. Snapshot is May 2025; not live allocations.

documents.title: PM-USHA Guidelines
documents.text: Covers government and government-aided higher education institutions of states/UTs. Gives priority to focus districts and defines components and eligibility. Eligibility and programme scope do not establish that an institution has received funding. Historical AISHE figures in the guidelines are not current counts.

documents.title: Population Projections for India and States 2011–2036
documents.text: Uses Census 2011, SRS fertility/mortality and migration assumptions. Projects total population increase and a decline in the national population aged 5–14 during 2011–2036. Projections are model-based rather than new census observations. Total population growth cannot substitute for school-age population growth. District/city downscaling requires separate validation. Mirrored copies surfaced differing summary totals; numeric population claims are intentionally omitted until document edition provenance is reconciled.

documents.title: Pratham Education Foundation Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Report describes direct learning programmes and district, city and state government partnerships. Report contains financials and supporters sections. Historical Mumbai municipal-school partnerships are documented. Self-reported programme reach is not a school funding receipt. Historical Mumbai narrative does not prove current city funding allocation. No financial totals from this report validated; full financial section not extracted in this pass.

documents.title: Quota for EWS Seats in Private Unaided Schools — Lok Sabha Question 1260
documents.text: Provides sanctioned and reimbursed-to-school amounts under RTE for Karnataka for five years. FY 2025-26 sanctioned ₹156.10 crore and reimbursed ₹148.68 crore. Government says reimbursement is timely, based on information from the state. Describes 2018 Karnataka neighbourhood-school exemption. Including Bengaluru does not make this city-level funding. The table covers the reimbursement claim population; do not interpret as uniquely new entry-grade admissions without checking definitions. Sanctioned less reimbursed does not establish overdue obligations or misuse. Distinct from central releases to the state; do not sum with Samagra central share as independent money.

documents.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
documents.text: Section 12(1)(c) provides entry-level admissions for eligible disadvantaged/weaker-section children of at least 25% in specified categories of schools. Section 12(2) provides private unaided school reimbursement capped at state per-child expenditure or actual charge, whichever is lower, with provisos for pre-existing free-education obligations. Not an unrestricted private-school capital grant. School eligibility, constitutional/applicability exclusions, neighbourhood rules and claims are determined by applicable law and state implementation. Statutory eligibility is not evidence of payment.

documents.title: Chhattisgarh Samagra Shiksha 2025-26 revised PAB minutes
documents.text: Approved annual work plan: ₹232,029.17 lakh including ₹82,492.13 lakh spillover. Planned central share to be released: ₹112,900.28 lakh; corresponding state share ₹75,267.52 lakh. Supplementary ICT labs and smart classrooms approval: ₹14,133.80 lakh. Supersedes sections of earlier 9 May 2025 minutes; preserve version history. The section heading says Actual Release, but the line explicitly says to be released: classify as planned/approved, not actual disbursement. Opening balances and spillover make the approved plan different from fresh allocations. OCR affects table layout; use explicit prose figures and reconcile original PDF before bulk extraction. Origin PDF returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-06; preserve indexed-text access status and locate replacement archive before treating as live-verified.

documents.title: Documents & Reports — Samagra Shiksha PAB minutes
documents.text: Provides state/UT financial-year entries with minutes, supplementary minutes, addenda and revisions. An index to retrieve further records, not extracted transaction coverage. Document links may move; origin link health must be checked. Index includes organisations as well as states, so row count is not geographic coverage.

documents.title: Tata Trusts Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Grant disbursal table reports ₹247.47 crore education institutional/direct implementation spend and ₹40.91 crore education individual grants. Report explicitly distinguishes institutional grants from individual grants. No city/state allocation derived from aggregate table. Institutional/direct implementation spend is broader than unrestricted school grants. These amounts should not be combined with NGO recipient disclosures without donor-recipient deduplication.

documents.title: Ministry of Education releases UDISE+ 2024-25 report
documents.text: Reports 104,125 single-teacher schools and 7,993 zero-enrolment schools in 2024-25. Reports total teachers 10,122,420. Reports computer access in 64.7% and internet in 63.5% of schools. National aggregate with mixed management categories; not a city-level finding. A zero-enrolment school is not necessarily a closed school. 2025-26 official parliamentary school-count data is newer.

documents.title: Report on UDISE+ 2023-24 — existing structure
documents.text: Separates government, government-aided, private unaided recognised, and other schools. Reports that student-wise collection from 2022-23 is not strictly comparable with earlier aggregate reporting for several education indicators. Historical methodology reference; not latest school data. Population denominator moderation can affect ratio comparisons. UDISE listing alone does not confer recognition.

documents.title: UP govt tells HC: No merger if school has over 50 students, 1km distance
documents.text: Reports extension of interim status quo for school pairing in Sitapur until 1 September 2025. Reports government assurances on enrolment/distance and court clarification that interim order does not affect overall policy. Historical interim procedural status, not current case disposition. Later court orders must be obtained before stating present legality or operative stay.

documents.title: Krishna Kumari and others v State of UP — 2025:AHC-LKO:38113
documents.text: Paragraph 3 identifies Government Order 16 June 2025 and consequent 24 June 2025 list of 105 schools challenged in petitions. Exa extract reviewed through early statutory discussion; final disposition not independently extracted. Subsequent appeal reporting exists; do not present this as final current case status.

documents.title: No merger for schools with 50 or more students as Uttar Pradesh government revises plan
documents.text: Reports minister's clarification excluding schools with 50 or more students and schools farther than 1km from pairing. Reports minister saying UDISE codes remain unchanged, buildings may host Bal Vatikas, and original classes can resume if enrolment/capacity warrants. Reported policy and explanation, not independent verification of implementation. Do not turn nearly 10,000 proposed pairings into confirmed permanent closures. Preserved codes mean stock series can miss changes in where teaching takes place.

documents.title: World Bank approves STARS to improve India's education system
documents.text: World Bank approved a USD 500 million STARS programme. Programme supports quality and governance of school education in six named states. Loan maturity 17.5 years including five-year grace period. Approval is not disbursement or per-state allocation. Source page extraction metadata says 2021-01-29 but article dateline is June 24, 2020; use dateline. Countrywide beneficiaries and six-state activities must not be treated as identical scope.

documents.title: STARS implementation status and results report, ISR59758
documents.text: Report states cumulative disbursement of USD 196.75 million (39.35%) against the USD 500 million programme. Report discusses programme restructuring and a requested extension. Historical snapshot, not current 2026 disbursement. Do not add disbursement to original loan value. A request for extension is not proof that an extension was approved.
